# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — Systemic Contract & Verification Fixes
- Changes I made:
  - `guidance.md`: Added "Core Output Contract: Literals Only" section explicitly forbidding formulas and Excel error strings, and requiring Python-side computation.
  - `prompt.md`: Added a mandatory "Verification Phase" to the operational policy, requiring explicit checks for formulas, error strings, and modification of untouched cells before finalizing.
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - **Formula Fix**: Targets the "Formula-instead-of-Value" cluster (e.g., 267-18, 54144). Expects the agent to compute values in Python. Safe because passing tasks already write literals.
  - **Error String Fix**: Targets the "Excel-Error-Text" cluster (e.g., 9569, 54144). Expects the agent to handle missing data in Python. Safe because passing tasks don't write error strings.
  - **Untouched Cells Fix**: Targets the "Untouched-Modified" cluster (e.g., 39046, 80-42). Expects the agent to verify the blast radius. Safe because passing tasks only touch target ranges.
- Building on prior RESULTS: This is the first iteration (seed). No prior results to build on.
- Refuted hypotheses: N/A.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: "Value-Mismatch" cluster (general logic errors). These require deeper method guidance or worked examples for complex spreadsheet logic.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Address the Value-Mismatch cluster by introducing worked examples for common complex manipulation patterns.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.650 Δ=+0.275 · fixed={31628, 37378, 37456, 45635, 46897, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59595, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={38462, 416-15, 560-12} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

## Iteration cand_0002 — Strengthening Blast Radius, Coverage, and Type Fidelity
- Changes I made:
  - `prompt.md`: Updated "Blast Radius Check" to forbid overwriting cells with identical content (targets Untouched-Modified cluster).
  - `prompt.md`: Added "Coverage Check" to the Verification Phase to prevent unintended empty cells in target ranges (targets Unintended-Empties cluster).
  - `prompt.md`: Updated "Type Check" to explicitly require `datetime` objects for dates/times, forbidding string representations (targets Type-Mismatch cluster).
  - `guidance.md`: Added "NO UNINTENDED EMPTIES" and reinforced "TYPE FIDELITY" (datetime objects) and "PRESERVE INPUTS".
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - **Blast Radius**: Expects agent to leave cells untouched if the value doesn't change. Safe because passing tasks already only modify targets.
  - **Coverage**: Expects agent to ensure all target cells that should have values are filled. Safe because passing tasks already provide complete answers.
  - **Type Fidelity**: Expects agent to use native Python `datetime` objects. Safe because passing tasks that deal with dates already use the correct types or don't use dates.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Built on `cand_0001` which established the Literals Only contract. These edits sharpen the behavioral guards around that contract.
- Refuted hypotheses: N/A.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: General Value Mismatch (logic errors) - these likely need worked examples for complex spreadsheet logic.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Introduce worked examples for complex data manipulation and aggregation patterns to address the Value-Mismatch cluster.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.650 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={38462, 416-15, 53383, 560-12} · broke={37456, 46897, 54144, 9569} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

## Iteration cand_0003 — Strengthening Type Fidelity and Range Discipline
- Changes I made:
  - `guidance.md`: Updated "TYPE FIDELITY" to forbid string representations of dates/numbers and forbid converting original text to numbers unless requested (targets Type Mismatch cluster).
  - `prompt.md`: Updated "Blast Radius Check" to forbid overwriting cells with identical content and forbid writing past target range (targets Blast Radius cluster).
  - `prompt.md`: Added "Coverage Check" to the Verification Phase to prevent unintended empties in target ranges (targets Coverage cluster).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - **Type Fidelity**: Expects agent to use native Python types (especially `datetime`) and preserve original text types. Safe because passing tasks already follow this.
  - **Blast Radius**: Expects agent to leave cells untouched if the value doesn't change and stay within bounds. Safe because passing tasks already only modify targets.
  - **Coverage**: Expects agent to ensure all target cells that should have values are filled. Safe because passing tasks already provide complete answers.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Built on `cand_0001`. Ignored `cand_0002`'s specific failures in Blast Radius/Coverage by using more explicit, imperative instructions in the Verification Phase rather than just guidance.
- Refuted hypotheses: N/A.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: General Value Mismatch (logic errors) - these require deeper method guidance or worked examples for complex spreadsheet logic.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Introduce worked examples for complex data manipulation and aggregation patterns to address the Value-Mismatch cluster.

## Iteration 4
- guidance.md: added explicit datetime type and "preserve original types" rule to fix TYPE_MISMATCH (e.g., 416-15, 560-12).
- guidance.md: sharpened "PRESERVE INPUTS" rule to explicitly forbid overwriting with the same value unless requested to fix PRESERVE_INPUT_VIOLATION (e.g., 39046, 38462).
- prompt.md: added "Preservation Check" and updated "Type Check" in the mandatory verification phase to enforce the above.
- Expected effect: Increase reward by fixing type mismatches and unnecessary cell modifications.
- Safe: These are additive rules that target specific failures seen in traces; passing tasks already satisfy them.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.550 Δ=-0.100 · fixed={227-40, 416-15} · broke={2768, 37456, 395-36, 46897, 54144, 9726} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

## Iteration cand_0005 — Strengthening Type Fidelity and Range Discipline
- Changes I made:
  - `guidance.md`: Updated "TYPE FIDELITY" to explicitly require `datetime.date` or `datetime.datetime` objects for dates/times, and warn against formatted strings.
  - `guidance.md`: Moved the "PRESERVE INPUTS" rule to the final verification checklist to make it a mandatory, unavoidable pre-save step.
  - `prompt.md`: Added a "Coordinate Adherence" rule to the Execution Phase, requiring the agent to explicitly calculate target boundaries and limit writes to those exact coordinates.
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - **Date Type Fix**: Targets "Type Mismatch" (e.g., 416-15). Expects agent to avoid string representations of dates. Safe because passing tasks already use correct types or don't write dates.
  - **Preserve Inputs Fix**: Targets "Unnecessary Modification" (e.g., 38462, 39046, 50768). Expects agent to verify and avoid overwriting cells with identical values. Safe because all passing tasks already preserve inputs.
  - **Range Discipline Fix**: Targets "Range/Boundary Error" (e.g., 560-12, 50768). Expects agent to stay strictly within `answer_position`. Safe because passing tasks already adhere to boundaries.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Built on `cand_0001` champion. Avoided the aggressive "Coverage Check" and "Preserve Original Types" rules from `cand_0002/0003/0004` that regressed high-value tasks (e.g., 54144, 9569).
- Refuted hypotheses: a prior RESULT (cand_0004) showed that purely additive prose rules about "preserving original types" can be over-aggressive and break tasks; therefore, I've focused on explicit coordinate boundaries and a pre-save checklist for input preservation.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: "Value-Mismatch" (logic errors). These are highly task-specific and would require a large set of worked examples to generalize.
- Plateau signal: The run has seen several rejects recently. Switching from "adding rules" to "adding structure" (checklist/coordinate boundaries) to make existing rules unavoidable.
- Focus next iteration: If this is the final iteration, no further focus. Otherwise, consider a small set of highly generalized worked examples for common calculation patterns.
